objective: Implement shared authored scene/settings transactions and an independently interrupted native Linux coherent-generation store without enabling unqualified product commit IPC or activation.
decisions: Embed the existing authored schema closure and preserve hierarchy, layout, binding, setting, revision and annotation semantics. Runtime validation neither fetches schemas nor accepts an alternate dialect.
Use one serialized coordinator, native-supplied authority, a mandatory resource preparer, current-policy checks and the existing bounded request ledger. Only one complete generation may publish.
Retain original principal/epoch/request/body identity in committed manifests. Typed reconciliation never resubmits the mutation, and durability never asserts visible activation.

Use private held directory handles, exclusive writer ownership, immutable generations, hashes and explicit current/previous selecting records. Corruption remains preserved and blocks writes pending repair.
Apply the final policy guard after temporary selector flush and just before native replacement. Report ambiguous publication as unknown and require reopening before further writes.
Keep the native experiment on an independently checked ext4 laboratory mount with synthetic configuration and typed policy. Bound attempts to 32 without automatic pruning.

Preserve initial undeclared-thread component failures and the historical import audit failure. Admit exactly four documented XP Kernel32 event APIs without changing the historical OS/runtime qualification claim.
Preserve all five required complete 0.1.0 desktop editions; this is an implementation prerequisite, not release completion.

limitations: W-08 remains in progress. The typed coordinator and finite storage probe do not enable command commits in existing IPC sessions.
The mandatory preparer in the native fixture accepts a synthetic built-in theme only. Installed resource closure, preset/migration, undo and external authoring conflict paths remain open.
Native ext4 process interruption and fsync acknowledgements do not qualify hardware power loss or arbitrary filesystems. The ext-family native magic check alone is not exact profile qualification.
